From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodai.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned runtime hotpatch & instance rotation — WestUS4 — Apr 22

Hi Sara / Acme team,

Heads-up from Infra/SRE: we have a coordinated runtime hotpatch and rolling instance rotation scheduled for region WestUS4 on Thu, Apr 22, 2027 between 02:00–05:00 PDT. This is a low-risk maintenance to apply a critical libc runtime hotpatch and rotate GPU-serving instances to pick up the updated runtime.

What to expect
- We will perform staged rotations per availability zone with graceful connection draining. Individual model endpoints may experience 1–3s additional cold-start latency during their turn; no hard downtime expected.
- Short-lived 30–90s request throttling windows may occur for heavy synchronous calls during zone handoffs.
- We will fallback traffic to compatible model variants if we detect request spikes.

Action items for Acme
- If you have scheduled nightly batch jobs between 01:30–03:30 PDT, please reply with any critical windows so we can avoid those minutes for your primary workloads.
- If you rely on pinned model artifact versions, confirm whether you want us to keep pinned instances out of rotation (tradeoff: delayed patching).

Attachments: rotation checklist + schedule (CSV) attached.
Runbook & post-maintenance: we will publish a short status note and the full postmortem if anything anomalous appears. Link to postmortem placeholder & ticket: JIRA INF-8721.

If you prefer a brief call during the window to watch the metrics, Marcus and I can join.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Program Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — appreciate the heads-up. Our nightly aggregation runs usually start at 02:00 PDT and last ~45 minutes. That's right in the middle of your window.

Can you either: 1) avoid rotating the zones that host our reserve pool until 03:30 PDT, or 2) shift the rotation for our routes to an earlier slot (23:00–01:00 PDT) if that is easier on your ops schedule?

We don't need pinned instances; patching is fine as long as there's minimal request throttling during our batch window. If there is an unavoidable overlap, please put us on the incident channel so our downstream pipeline can auto-retry.

—Sara
Sara Cho
Platform Ops, Acme Analytics

Proposal:
- Keep the rotation schedule as-is but mark Acme's primary IP pool as "defer until 03:30" in the rotation CSV. This will delay patch for their nodes by ~90m.
- Ensure we enable prefix caching for their high-throughput endpoints during the handoff to reduce throttling impact.
- Assign a named incident channel and add Sara + acme-support; Marcus will join exec watch.

Checklist highlights in attachment — be sure graceful drain timeout = 120s for these instances and health-check retries = 3. If you need me to call Acme, I can do a 10-min alignment.

Evelyn

Subject: Completed: runtime hotpatch & instance rotation — WestUS4 — summary

Hi Sara / Acme team — quick summary from the maintenance window (completed).

What we did
- Applied libc hotpatch across runtime containers and rotated serving instances in WestUS4 with staged AZ handoffs.
- For Acme's primary pool we deferred rotation until 03:30 PDT as requested; those instances were rotated during the tail of the window with graceful drains (120s).

Observed impact
- No customer-facing errors reported. We saw transient latency spikes of 1.5–3.2s for synchronous gen calls on two endpoints during their zone handoff. No failed requests attributed to the rotation; retries handled the brief throttling.
- Background batch jobs that overlapped experienced built-in retries and completed successfully after a brief delay.

Follow-up items (we will own/track)
- INF-8721: add auto-adjusted drainage rules for customers with scheduled batch windows (owner: Jonas Weber).
- Postmortem doc published: https://redwood.company/docs/postmortem/RT-2027-045
- We will push a minor runtime improvement to reduce cold-starts for pinned models (planned May 3).

If you'd like a short post-maintenance review call, Marcus and I are available this afternoon.

Thanks for the coordination and for flagging your batch window — that helped avoid customer-visible disruption.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Program Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
